tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Use this tool if you need to view the contents of an existing file

parameters.name: filepath
parameters.description: The path of the file to read. Can be a relative path (from workspace root), absolute path, tilde path (~/...), or file:// URI

tools.returnsDescription: The file contents as a string

tools.name: create_new_file
tools.description: Create a new file. Only use this when a file doesn't exist and should be created

parameters.name: filepath
parameters.description: The path where the new file should be created. Can be a relative path (from workspace root), absolute path, tilde path (~/...), or file:// URI

parameters.name: contents
parameters.description: The contents to write to the new file

tools.returnsDescription: Confirmation that the file was created successfully

tools.name: run_terminal_command
tools.description: Run a terminal command in the current directory. The shell is not stateful and will not remember any previous commands. When a command is run in the background ALWAYS suggest to the user that they should use the Run Code tool if the process is still running (may take a while)

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: The command to run. This will be passed directly into the IDE shell

parameters.name: waitForCompletion
parameters.description: Whether to wait for the command to complete before returning. Default is true. Set to false to run the command in the background and collect output asynchronously

tools.returnsDescription: Standard output and error from the command

tools.name: file_glob_search
tools.description: Search for files recursively in the project using glob patterns. Supports ** for recursive directory search. Will not show many build, cache, secrets dirs/files (can use ls to view them directly)

parameters.name: pattern
parameters.description: Glob pattern for file path matching (e.g., '**/*.cs', '**/test/**/*.cs')

tools.returnsDescription: List of file paths matching the glob pattern

tools.name: view_diff
tools.description: View the current diff of working changes
tools.returnsDescription: The unified diff of all current changes

tools.name: read_currently_open_file
tools.description: Read the currently open file in the IDE. If the user seems to be referring to a file that you can't see, or is requesting an action on content that seems missing, try using this tool
tools.returnsDescription: The contents of the currently open file in the IDE

tools.name: ls
tools.description: List files and folders in a given directory

parameters.name: dirPath
parameters.description: The directory path. Can be relative to project root, absolute path, tilde path (~/...), or file:// URI. Use forward slash paths

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: If true, lists files and folders recursively. To prevent unexpected large results, use this sparingly

tools.returnsDescription: List of file and folder names in the directory

tools.name: create_rule_block
tools.description: Creates a 'rule' that can be referenced in future conversations. This should be used whenever you want to establish code standards / preferences that should be applied consistently across a project

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Short, descriptive name summarizing the rule's purpose (e.g. 'React Standards', 'Type Hints')

parameters.name: rule
parameters.description: Clear, imperative instruction for future conversations

tools.returnsDescription: Confirmation that the rule was created and can now be referenced

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Edit or replace specific lines in an existing file. Provide the old text to find and the new text to replace with

parameters.name: filepath
parameters.description: The path of the file to edit. Can be relative or absolute

parameters.name: oldText
parameters.description: The exact text to find and replace (must include surrounding context)

parameters.name: newText
parameters.description: The new text to replace oldText with

tools.returnsDescription: Confirmation of the edit operation

tools.name: search_codebase
tools.description: Search the codebase for matches to a query. Can use regex patterns or literal text matching

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: The search query or regex pattern

parameters.name: maxResults
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return

tools.returnsDescription: List of matching code snippets with file paths and line numbers

tools.name: run_pytest
tools.description: Run pytest test suite to verify code changes

parameters.name: testPath
parameters.description: Path to test file or directory to run. If empty, runs all tests

tools.returnsDescription: Test results including passed, failed, and skipped counts

tools.name: get_problems
tools.description: Get compiler errors, warnings, and IDE problems for the current project
tools.returnsDescription: List of problems with file paths, line numbers, severity, and messages

tools.name: view_file
tools.description: View a file with line numbers for easier reference. Better for viewing full files

parameters.name: filepath
parameters.description: The path of the file to view

tools.returnsDescription: File contents with line number prefixes

tools.name: open_file
tools.description: Open a file in the IDE editor for viewing or editing

parameters.name: filepath
parameters.description: The path of the file to open

tools.returnsDescription: Confirmation that the file was opened in the IDE

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Show git status of the repository including modified files, staged changes, and untracked files
tools.returnsDescription: Git status output showing current branch and file changes

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Show git diff of current changes in the repository

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Optional. Specific file to show diff for. If empty, shows all diffs

tools.returnsDescription: Unified diff format showing additions and deletions

tools.name: git_log
tools.description: Show git commit history of the repository

parameters.name: maxCommits
parameters.description: Maximum number of commits to show

tools.returnsDescription: Commit history with hashes, authors, dates, and messages

tools.name: git_commit
tools.description: Create a git commit with the given message

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Commit message describing the changes

tools.returnsDescription: Confirmation of the commit with commit hash

tools.name: create_snippet
tools.description: Create a reusable code snippet for future reference or insertion

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the snippet for easy reference

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The code content of the snippet

tools.returnsDescription: Confirmation that the snippet was created

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Create a new directory/folder. Only use this when a directory doesn't exist and should be created

parameters.name: folderpath
parameters.description: The path where the new folder should be created. Can be a relative path (from workspace root), absolute path, tilde path (~/...), or file:// URI

tools.returnsDescription: Confirmation that the folder was created successfully

tools.name: read_plan
tools.description: Read the active plan file (the plan the user has open under ~/.continueVS/plans/, bound at send time). Use this to pull up the current plan so you can work through its steps. If a plan is bound, it is read by default; you may pass an explicit 'path' (repo-root-relative) to read a different plan. If there is no bound plan and no path, this returns an explicit 'no active plan' signal.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Optional. Repo-root-relative path to a plan file. If omitted, the bound (active) plan is used.

tools.returnsDescription: The full plan text plus the plan file it came from

tools.name: update_plan
tools.description: Update the active plan file (the plan bound at send time under ~/.continueVS/plans/) with an exact find/replace. The plan text you read is the 'find' and the 'replace' is what it becomes. You manage your own pass/fail markers (e.g. replacing '⏳' with '✅' as steps complete). 'find' must match exactly. Returns the number of matches replaced, so if your 'find' is wrong you get count 0 and can correct it. Optionally pass an explicit 'path' (repo-root-relative) to update a different plan.

parameters.name: find
parameters.description: The exact text in the plan to search for. Must match exactly.

parameters.name: replace
parameters.description: The text to replace every exact match of 'find' with.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Optional. Repo-root-relative path to a plan file. If omitted, the bound (active) plan is used.

tools.returnsDescription: The number of matches replaced and where

tools.name: ask_user
tools.description: Ask the user a question when you need information, clarification, or confirmation to continue. Use this ONLY when you genuinely cannot proceed without a user decision; prefer acting autonomously when you have enough context. Provide 'question' (the text to ask) and, if there is a limited set of reasonable choices, provide 'answers' (a list of suggested answer options). The user may pick one of the provided options or type their own free-text response. If no answers are supplied, the question is open-ended and the user will respond in prose.

parameters.name: question
parameters.description: The question to present to the user. Required.

parameters.name: answers
parameters.description: Optional list of suggested answer options (multiple choice). The user may pick one or type their own. Omit for an open-ended question.

tools.returnsDescription: The user's answer to the question as a string

tools.name: debug_start
tools.description: Start (launch) a new debugging session. If project is empty the solution's startup project is used; launchProfile selects a launch profile (empty = default).

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: Project to start. Empty uses the solution startup project.

parameters.name: launchProfile
parameters.description: Launch profile to use. Empty uses the default.

tools.returnsDescription: The started debug session handle and its mode

tools.name: debug_stop
tools.description: Stop the currently active debugging session and clear the selected session binding.
tools.returnsDescription: The ended debug session handle, or an indication that none was running

tools.name: debug_restart
tools.description: Restart the current debugging session: stop any active session then start it again.
tools.returnsDescription: The restarted debug session handle

tools.name: ide_attach_to_process
tools.description: Attach the debugger to a running local process by its OS process id (pid), then select that attached session for subsequent debug_* tools.

parameters.name: processId
parameters.description: The OS process id to attach to.

tools.returnsDescription: The attached debug session handle and its mode

tools.name: debug_select_session
tools.description: Select (bind) a debug session by its session id so subsequent debug_* tools act on it.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The session id (e.g. 'proc:1234') to select.

tools.returnsDescription: The bound debug session handle
